name: Valsartan
route_note: oral tablet or solution once or twice daily
owner: generic (many); Diovan brand held by Novartis

discovery.note: A non-heterocyclic sartan developed in Basel.

tagline: Blockbuster ARB at the centre of the 2018 nitrosamine contamination recall
summary: Valsartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker used for hypertension, heart failure and left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction. It is also a component of sacubitril/valsartan, and in 2018 contaminated generic supplies triggered a global recall.
mechanism: Angiotensin II receptor blockers selectively block the AT1 receptor, preventing angiotensin II from causing vasoconstriction, aldosterone release, sympathetic activation and sodium retention. Because ACE is not inhibited, bradykinin does not accumulate, so cough is uncommon.
Valsartan is active as given and is excreted largely unchanged in bile, so it has few metabolic drug interactions.
uses: Left ventricular failure or dysfunction after myocardial infarction

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Diovan.

history.title: Val-HeFT
history.detail: Valsartan reduces heart failure hospitalisation when added to standard therapy.

history.title: VALIANT
history.detail: Valsartan is as effective as captopril after MI with heart failure or LV dysfunction.

history.title: Japanese data scandal
history.detail: Papers from Japanese investigator-led valsartan trials are retracted after data manipulation involving a Novartis employee.

history.title: US generics
history.detail: Generic valsartan launches in the US.

history.title: NDMA recall
history.detail: Valsartan made with active ingredient from a Chinese supplier is found to contain the probable carcinogen NDMA, prompting worldwide recalls and new nitrosamine controls.

serious: Acute kidney injury (especially with renal artery stenosis)
safety.boxed_warning: Fetal toxicity: drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus; discontinue when pregnancy is detected.

facts: The 2018 contamination led regulators worldwide to require nitrosamine risk assessments for all medicines.
